question: What is order to pod assignment?
context:
3.2 Order-to-Pod Assignment Problem Formulation Instead of assigning the order to the picking stations, each order will be assigned to a pod. Different from the previous related work, orders would be assigned to the picking station first, and then the required pod will be called to fulfill the order. However, it seems to be inefficient and will cause some restrictions if a picking station can only open up to three or six bins to place the ordered items, and when the orders need to be assigned to the picking stations, it will have the limitation of the number of bins for the order assignment. Instead of doing that, considering the flexibility of system resources [43], assuming the picking station can handle any order, the assignment between orders to the picking station is omitted, and the direct assignment for orders to pods can increase the possibility to optimize the order picking process. In this section, the scenarios of order -to-pod assignment and the formulation of optimization problem are illustrated in detail. 21 3.2.1 Scenario There are three scenarios for order-to-pod assignment: first come first served (FCFS) assignment, order batching assignment, and two -phase assignment. The detailed descriptions are as follows.
---
23 Figure 3.3 Order batching assignment flow chart The third scenario is the proposed two -phase assignment. Same as the order batching assignment, this assignment handles a group of orders at once. The main difference between order batching assignment and two -phase assignment is the system will identify the pod status and release parts of orders to the pods which have already been assigned to other orders before doing the order ba tching. The flow chart of the two-phase assignment is shown in Figure 3.4. 24 Figure 3.4 Two-phase assignment flow chart In order to identify the status of pods, the sy stem will differentiate the availability of pods in different steps. The status of pods is classified based on it is available to be assigned or not, and it could be divided into 6 different statuses, including:  Assigned pod - Static pod: waiting to be picked by robot 25 - En-route pod: from storage area to the picking station - Queueing pod: waiting in the queue - Picking pod: picked by picker at the picking station  Unassigned pod - Idle pod: no assignment yet - Returning pod: after being picked, on the way back to the s torage area The pod will have different statuses in the moving processes. When the pod is in the storage area and hasn’t been assigned to any order, at this point it is in an “idle pod” status. After it is assigned to orders, the status will be turned into “assigned pod” and wait to be picked by a robot, so it is classified as “static pod”. When the robot arrives and picks the pod, it will be brought to the picking station from the storage area, and the status will be “en-route pod”. After the pod reaches the picking station, it may need to wait for other pods to be processed in the queue, so the status is “queueing pod”. When the pod is picked by the picker in the picking station, the status will change into “picking pod” and not allow to be assigned anymor e at this point. After the pod is done in the picking station, the robot will bring it back to the empty location of the storage area, and the status will be “returning pod”. And the pod will be idle again after it is put back in the storage area.

The cycl e of the pod status is shown in Figure 3.5. 26 Figure 3.5 The cycle of the pod status As for the overall process of the two-phase assignment scenario, after the order arrival and sorting. As shown in Figure 3.4, in Phase 1, the system will first identify the pod status and search for the assigned pods. If there are some orders that match the assigned pods, they will be assigned to those pods. In Phase 2, after releasing orders to the assigned pods, if there are some orders left, they will only be assigned to the unassigned pods, which are those still idle in the storage area

The order-to-pod assignment is a research scenario where each order is directly assigned to a pod instead of being assigned to a picking station first. This approach aims to increase the possibility to optimize the order picking process by considering system resources flexibility.

There are three scenarios for this assignment:

1. First Come First Served (FCFS) Assignment
2. Order Batching Assignment 
3. Two-Phase Assignment

The two-phase assignment is the proposed scenario where a group of orders is handled at once. The main difference between order batching and two-phase assignment is that, in the two-phase assignment, the system identifies the pod status before doing the order batching.

In this process, pods have different statuses such as "Assigned Pod", "En-route Pod", "Queueing Pod", "Picking Pod" or "Returning Pod". The cycle of a pod's status is shown in Figure 3.5.

The overall process of the two-phase assignment scenario starts with order arrival and sorting. In Phase 1, the system identifies the pod status and searches for assigned pods to assign orders to them. If there are some orders left after releasing them to the assigned pods, they will only be assigned to unassigned pods in Phase 2 which are those still idle in the storage area.

This approach aims to optimize the order picking process by considering system resources flexibility.

The constraints ensure that all the orders could be covered by the assigned pod (Equation 2), each order needs to be assigned to one pod (Equation 3), the order should be assigned to the same pod as its SKU (Equation 4), and the total quantity of SKU in an assigned pod should not exceed the sum of quantities of SKU in the assigned orders (Equation 5). Order batching is a method in warehouse management and order picking processes that aims to minimize traveling time and distance. It involves grouping a set of customer orders into picking orders, also known as order batches. This strategy reduces the number of times order pickers need to travel between storage locations and the picking area, thereby minimizing travel time and distance.

There are two types of batching based on the availability of customer order information:

1. Static Batching: The characteristics of each customer order (requested items and quantities) are known when the batching decision is made.
2. Dynamic Batching: Customer orders arrive stochastically, with information about them becoming available only when they have arrived.

The criteria for batching include proximity of pick locations and time windows:

1. Proximity Batching: Orders are assigned to a batch based on their storage location's proximity. The goal is to minimize processing time such as total traveling time, distance, or maximum lead time.
2. Time Window Batching: Orders arriving during the same fixed or variable length time interval (time window) are grouped together and processed simultaneously in the following stages.

Order batching aims to reduce operating costs by improving warehouse efficiency through reduced travel times and distances.

Order batching is a method in warehouse management and order picking processes that aims to minimize traveling time and distance. It involves grouping a set of customer orders into picking orders, also known as order batches. This strategy reduces the number of times order pickers need to travel between storage locations and the picking area, thereby minimizing travel time and distance.

There are two types of batching based on the availability of customer order information:

1. Static Batching: The characteristics of each customer order (requested items and quantities) are known when the batching decision is made.
2. Dynamic Batching: Customer orders arrive stochastically, with information about them becoming available only when they have arrived.

The criteria for batching include proximity of pick locations and time windows:

1. Proximity Batching: Orders are assigned to a batch based on their storage location's proximity. The goal is to minimize processing time such as total traveling time, distance, or maximum lead time.
2. Time Window Batching: Orders arriving during the same fixed or variable length time interval (time window) are grouped together and processed simultaneously in the following stages.

Order batching aims to reduce operating costs by improving warehouse efficiency through reduced travel times and distances.

- Unassigned pod: Idle pod, Returning pod

2. Static pod (waiting to be picked by a robot): After assigned to orders.

4. Queueing pod: When the pod reaches the picking station and may need to wait for other pods to be processed in the queue.
5. Picking pod: When the pod is picked by the picker in the picking station.
6. Returning pod: After the pod is done in the picking station, the robot brings it back to the empty location of the storage area.

This cycle continues until all orders are assigned and picked or there are no more orders left to be processed.
